name: Nex Directory – Events Calendar, Business Directory, Job Board & Classifieds
author: Alex Player

sections.description:
Every town, scene and community has the same problem. The good stuff is scattered across group chats, social feeds and a spreadsheet somebody stopped updating, so nobody can find it.

Nex Directory gives it one home on your own WordPress site: a place where people can search what is on, see it on a map, save it for later and add their own.

Tell the setup wizard what you are building and the whole plugin changes to fit. The wording, the cards, the filters, the listing pages and even the main button are different for an events site, a local directory, a jobs board and a marketplace.

There is no listing limit. The WordPress.org plugin has no three-listing or three-event cap. Publish as many as you like.

See it running

These three sites run on this free plugin and the Twenty Twenty-Five theme:

  • Patchwork Bristol: a community what’s-on guide
  • The Pass: a hospitality jobs board
  • Wornwell Market: a vintage marketplace

Or click Live Preview at the top of this page to open a private test site in your browser. Nothing is installed on your own site.

Pick the site you are building

  • Events: a date on every card, filters for Today, This weekend and Free, RSVP with capacity and a waitlist, an add-to-calendar button and calendar feeds.
  • Local directory: live “Open now” status from opening hours, price level, services, amenities, and one-tap Call, Directions and Website buttons.
  • Jobs: pay shown up front, job type and remote/hybrid filters, closing dates, company details and an Apply now button.
  • Marketplace: price, condition, Reserved and Sold badges, Make an offer, delivery and collection options, and buy-safely tips.

You can switch type later in Settings, and rename any label: “Events” can be “Gigs”, “Listings” can be “Places”.

For your visitors: finding things is the easy part

  • A search box plus one-tap filter chips that change with the site type
  • A filter sheet for everything else, with clear zero-result screens
  • Grid, list and full-screen map views; on phones the map gets a draggable list
  • Month, week and agenda calendar views
  • Hearts to save anything, with an Undo toast; signed-in users’ saves follow them between devices

On phones it behaves like an app rather than a squashed desktop page: a bottom tab bar, bottom sheets, swipeable photos and a sticky action bar.

For the people who post: no wp-admin needed

  • A simple “add a listing” flow that asks for the essentials first, with auto-saving drafts
  • A personal workspace: what’s coming up, every listing in one table with bulk actions, messages and saved items
  • Event tools: attendee lists, RSVP and waitlist management, check-in mode and a share kit with a QR code
  • Owner editing, claim-a-listing requests and moderation with reviewer notes

For you: set it up once, then just approve

  • A setup wizard that asks what you’re building, then creates the pages and settings for you
  • A dashboard with charts and a keyboard-friendly inbox for submissions, claims and reports
  • Settings with a live preview: brand colour, fonts, card style and page template
  • Roles and permissions, email verification, a honeypot, rate limits and optional reCAPTCHA
  • CSV and JSON imports with a preview, and optional demo content that only imports when you confirm it
  • Shortcodes and Elementor widgets for putting any view on any page

It looks like you hired a designer

Choose from 12 listing-page templates (Clarity, Immersive, Cinematic, Editorial, Conference, Festival, Split, Minimal, Venue, Compact, Job and Product) and 7 card styles, including Classic, Poster, Spotlight and Glass. Each listing page has a photo gallery with a lightbox, maps and directions, the host or seller, related listings, share buttons and a sticky action bar on phones.

Nex Directory’s pages are styled with their own scoped CSS, so they look the same in any theme. Set your brand colour and font once and they apply everywhere.

Already using another plugin? Bring your listings with you

A five-step wizard brings your listings over from Directorist, GeoDirectory, HivePress, WP Job Manager, The Events Calendar, Events Manager, Modern Events Calendar, EventON, Event Organiser, All-in-One Event Calendar, Sugar Calendar, Eventin or WP Event Manager. It copies details, dates in the right time zone, venues, contact details, opening hours, categories and images, never changes your old data, and redirects your old listing URLs so links and search rankings carry over. You can also import any CSV or JSON file, including opening hours written in plain English.

For agencies and developers

Nex Directory includes shortcodes, Elementor widgets, REST endpoints for approved integrations, filters and actions, and readable CSS and JavaScript with design tokens, so you can restyle it without fighting it. No build step is needed to install or run it.

Optional Chrome extension

The plugin includes a Chrome Extension setup screen for the official Nex Directory Scanner. It shows connection status, recent activity, policy checks, and a secure connection key you can rotate.

Official Nex Directory Chrome extension:

https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/nexdirectory-scanner/dnijcccaedhkbbekcbacgbhldmminpip

The extension is optional. Nex Directory opens the Chrome Web Store only when an administrator clicks the download link.

Optional Pro add-on

Nex Directory Pro is a separate add-on for sites that need more advanced workflows, such as AI-assisted setup, custom templates, advanced fields and filters, private attending calendars, ticketing, paid boosts, QR check-in, analytics exports, team tools, white-label controls, and search indexing hooks.

Those Pro tools and any services they use are not bundled in this WordPress.org plugin. The directory, event, submission, moderation, map, calendar, and member features listed here continue to work without Pro.

External services

Nex Directory avoids contacting outside providers unless a related optional feature is configured, shown on the page, or deliberately clicked. These notes explain what may be shared when you choose to use those features. Requests can include normal browser data such as IP address, browser details, and referrer, along with the feature-specific data described below.

NexDirectory.com and Chrome Web Store

NexDirectory.com receives normal browser request data only when an administrator clicks a product, documentation, or support link. The Chrome Web Store receives the same type of data after an administrator clicks the extension download link.

NexDirectory terms: https://nexdirectory.com/terms-of-service/
NexDirectory privacy: https://nexdirectory.com/privacy-policy/
Google terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
Google privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Google services

reCAPTCHA loads only after a site owner configures it; browser data and verification tokens are sent to Google. Google Maps and geocoding are used only when selected and can receive an API key, entered location, coordinates, or map position. Clicking “Directions” or “Open in Google Maps” on a listing opens Google Maps with that listing’s address or coordinates. Clicking “Google Calendar” sends the listing title, dates, description, and location to Google Calendar. Opening a Google Docs preview sends the document URL to Google Docs Viewer.

Google terms/privacy: https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
Google Maps terms: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms

Map, tile, and geocoding providers

Maps load their tiles from the provider the site owner selects: Esri (ArcGIS Online basemaps, used by the default Modern light, Minimal grey and Dark styles), OpenStreetMap, OSM France HOT, OpenTopoMap, Mapbox, Google Maps or a custom provider. Map/tile requests can include map position, tile coordinates, zoom level and entered location text. Server-side geocoding sends location text; Mapbox validation can send the configured token and style path.

OpenStreetMap policies/privacy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ and https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy
Nominatim policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/
OSM France terms: https://www.openstreetmap.fr/mentions-legales/
OpenTopoMap usage: https://opentopomap.org/about
Mapbox terms/privacy: https://www.mapbox.com/legal/tos and https://www.mapbox.com/legal/privacy/
Esri terms/privacy: https://www.esri.com/en-us/legal/terms/full-master-agreement and https://www.esri.com/en-us/privacy/overview

Calendar links

Clicking “Outlook” or “Office 365” in an add-to-calendar menu opens Microsoft Outlook on the web and sends the listing title, dates, description and location to Microsoft. Nothing is sent until a visitor clicks. (Google Calendar is covered under Google services above.)

Microsoft terms/privacy: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement

Web fonts (off by default)

The default font, Inter, is bundled with the plugin. If a developer enables the nexdirectory_load_remote_web_fonts filter to use another font, the visitor’s browser requests that font from Bunny Fonts (fonts.bunny.net), which receives normal browser request data.

Bunny Fonts terms/privacy: https://bunny.net/tos/ and https://bunny.net/privacy/

Media previews and sharing

When an owner adds YouTube or Vimeo media, the provider can receive normal browser request data when its thumbnail/player loads or a visitor opens it. Google Docs previews are covered above. Clicking a Facebook, X, LinkedIn or WhatsApp share control sends the public listing URL and, where supported, its title to that provider.

YouTube terms/privacy: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
Vimeo terms/privacy: https://vimeo.com/terms and https://vimeo.com/privacy
Facebook terms/privacy: https://www.facebook.com/terms/ and https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
X terms/privacy: https://x.com/en/tos and https://x.com/en/privacy
LinkedIn terms/privacy: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement and https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy
WhatsApp terms/privacy: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy

Source code and build tools

All plugin-owned PHP, JavaScript, and CSS needed to inspect and modify the release is included. No build step is required to install or run it.

Bundled third-party browser libraries are versioned upstream runtime files. Exact versions, licenses, and public source URLs are listed in docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md. The portable source and commands for regenerating the Tailwind utility bundle are in docs/SOURCE_AND_BUILD.md.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the nexdirectory folder, or install Nex Directory from WordPress.org.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open the Nex Directory setup wizard.
  4. Choose a starter template, or build your directory manually.
  5. Review the pages Nex Directory creates and adjust your settings in WP Admin -> Nex Directory.
sections.faq:
Can I try it before installing?

Yes. Click “Live Preview” at the top of this page. It opens a free, private test site in your browser with Nex Directory and sample events already set up. Nothing is installed on your own site.

How many listings or events can I publish?

Nex Directory does not add a three-item publishing cap. You can publish as many listings or events as your site, hosting, storage, roles, and moderation settings allow.

Do I need Pro to publish more content?

No. Pro adds advanced workflows and integrations, but it is not needed to publish more listings or events.

Is Nex Directory only for events?

No. Pick Events, Local directory, Jobs or Marketplace in the setup wizard and the cards, filters, listing pages and buttons change to fit. You can switch later in Settings, and rename any label to suit your site.

Can I move my listings from another plugin?

Yes. Go to Nex Directory › Import & export › Move from another plugin. It supports Directorist, GeoDirectory, HivePress, WP Job Manager, The Events Calendar, Events Manager, Modern Events Calendar, EventON, Event Organiser, All-in-One Event Calendar, Sugar Calendar, Eventin and WP Event Manager, even if that plugin is switched off. Your old data isn’t changed, and old listing URLs redirect to the new pages. Tickets, bookings and reviews from other plugins aren’t copied.

Will it work with my theme?

Yes. Nex Directory’s pages are self-contained and styled with their own scoped CSS, so they look the same in any theme. You can set your brand colour and font in Settings, and they apply everywhere.

Does it work well on phones?

Yes. Phones get a dedicated layout rather than a squashed desktop one, with a bottom tab bar, bottom sheets for filters and details, swipeable photo galleries and a sticky action bar.

Will demo content import automatically?

No. Demo content is optional and only imports after an administrator confirms it in the setup flow.

Do I need coding skills?

No. You can use the guided setup, ready-made pages, shortcodes, and settings screens without writing code. Developers can still customize the output when a project needs more control.

Does Nex Directory work with Elementor?

Yes. The plugin includes Elementor widgets for the included shortcodes.

Does it support maps and calendar subscriptions?

Yes. The WordPress.org plugin includes interactive map discovery plus public site and organizer iCalendar feeds. Private personal attending-calendar subscriptions are part of the separate Pro add-on.

Is the Chrome extension required?

No. It is optional. The connection screen provides setup guidance and links directly to the official Chrome Web Store listing.

Can I uninstall and remove all data?

Yes. Nex Directory includes an uninstall cleanup setting that can remove plugin data when the plugin is deleted.
sections.changelog:
1.7.0

  • Fixed: schedules, speakers and custom fields could be lost or garbled on save (a quotation mark emptied the whole schedule; “1–24” was stored as “1u201324”). Existing data is repaired once, with the original kept.
  • Fixed: session times, the calendar, the account agenda, job closing times and structured data were shifted by the site’s UTC offset on sites not set to UTC; the Today, Tomorrow and This weekend filters could be a day out.
  • Fixed: opening hours that run past midnight now show as one range and count as open after midnight; open-now uses the place’s own time zone.
  • Fixed: duplicating a listing kept its country and other fields and no longer damages the copied schedule; recurring copies too.
  • Fixed: grid, bento and search blocks were empty on job, directory and marketplace sites.
  • Fixed: on phones, a site-wide default of “map” no longer hides the title, search and results behind a full-screen map.
  • Fixed: the Location map on listing pages follows Settings › Maps. It is drawn with your chosen map tiles, and a Google Maps frame is only used when Google is your provider.
  • Fixed: the phone tab bar respects the log-in link settings; “&” no longer appears in category names on the map list; email subjects no longer show codes such as ““”.
  • Fixed: the system health check no longer warns about reminder emails on sites that do not send them; a scheduled task is now removed when the plugin is deactivated or deleted.
  • Fixed: boosted listings now show their “Featured” badge and highlight on cards and the map (with the Pro add-on).
  • Fixed: CSV imports keep schedules and speakers whose text contains quotation marks, and the plugin’s own export re-imports intact; a row with an unreadable date is reported instead of being published; far fewer empty fields are stored per imported listing.
  • Fixed: a late session that runs past midnight shows plain times; attendee counts use thousands separators; the place line is no longer printed twice; pay is no longer repeated in the job card.
  • New: “Make an offer” on marketplace items has its own form with an amount, and the seller’s message starts with the offer.
  • New: event pages show an “Open event app” button when an add-on provides an app for the event, in every page template.
  • Improved: after submitting, people land on their new listing in the workspace; the events home page is titled “Just announced”; the agenda log-in hint only appears on real programmes.
  • New: attendees are emailed when their RSVP is confirmed, when they join a waitlist and when a place opens up for them (Settings › Notifications).
  • New: raising an event’s capacity moves people off the waitlist in order.
  • Improved: list view uses the full width on wide screens, and the footer and card grid can be restyled from a theme with custom properties (see docs/design-language.md).
  • Improved: an event that has ended no longer accepts RSVPs; two people can work the door in check-in mode without overwriting each other.
  • Developers: new filters nexdirectory_rsvp_join_allowed, nexdirectory_single_show_free_rsvp_with_tickets, nexdirectory_submitter_dashboard_allowed_pages, nexdirectory_mobile_tabbar_tabs, nexdirectory_send_attendee_rsvp_email, nexdirectory_rsvp_leave_allowed, nexdirectory_account_show_boosts_tab and action nexdirectory_render_extension_account_event_actions.
  • Fixed: replies in the workspace inbox were always refused with “Message content is required”; they now send.
  • Fixed: everyone in the inbox was shown as “Member” instead of by name.
  • Fixed: “Apply by email” on a job put codes such as “&” in the email subject when the job title had an ampersand or quotation marks.
  • New: “Mark as sold” and “Mark as available” in the desktop menu of each marketplace item in the workspace (it was only in the phone menu).
  • Fixed: on marketplace sites a private seller editing their own item found the address box empty and could not save without retyping it. The rule that hides a private seller’s street address from visitors was also hiding it from the owner.
  • Fixed: category groups stored by the Pro add-on were not registered and caused a PHP warning on every page.
  • New: the submission form has a place for add-on questions again (it was lost in the 1.5.0 redesign).
  • Improved: on phones the action bar on a listing page sits on the bottom edge instead of floating above it.
  • Improved: page links (1, 2, Next) stay readable whatever your brand colours are, and no longer sit inside a second box.
  • Improved: “More like this” cards show the price and Sold or Reserved; short worded prices such as “Pay what you can” now show on cards.
  • Improved: marketplace item pages no longer show the seller’s view count or empty facts (“Accepts offers: No”, “Quantity: 1”, “Returns accepted: No”).
  • Improved: on events sites the map list opens “Soonest first”; a search with nothing to pin no longer shows a map of the whole world.
  • Improved: online-only listings no longer show a street map and Directions.
  • Improved: icons beside short lists match the words or are a plain tick, instead of unrelated icons.
  • Improved: the search widget’s dropdowns and date field are labelled and styled, and its Reset button is readable (the label was white on white).
  • Improved: workspace cards on phones no longer start a line with a stray dot; the Inbox count in the page header updates after each action.
  • Fixed: with a custom display font, the navigation and whole page sections were set in the display font; it now applies to headings only.
  • Fixed: page 2 of a “What’s new” page stays on that page instead of jumping to the main listings page.
  • Fixed: the calendar’s event count counted an event once for every day it runs.
  • Improved: a short hero image no longer shows a dark strip under the header when the page is scrolled.
  • Improved: the Conference layout shows the price and places left on desktop; the Split layout has “Make an offer”; a job’s “About the company” shows the company logo.
  • Fixed: the “Live” switch in the organiser workspace now works. Flipping it changed how it looked but nothing was saved.
  • New: hooks for add-ons that hold a submission until a condition is met, such as a listing fee (nexdirectory_submission_post_status, nexdirectory_submission_held_redirect, nexdirectory_live_toggle_blocked_message, nexdirectory_render_extension_account_listings_notice). Nothing changes unless an add-on uses them.

1.6.1

  • Fixed: Live Preview on WordPress.org could fail to activate the plugin.
  • Fixed: setup-wizard redirects no longer interrupt background tasks, form submissions or network administration.

1.6.0

  • New: a simpler admin menu. 17 items became 7 (Home, Inbox, your listings, Members, Insights, Settings, Tools); every old link still works.
  • New: the whole site uses your site type’s words (Items, Events, Jobs or Places), with a Words panel to rename them.
  • New: grouped Settings with search, sample content you can remove with Undo, and a clearer setup wizard.
  • New: map previews open on hover, fill the card and lead with the price; nearby pins group instead of overlapping.
  • Improved: listing pages use 2-3 columns for short lists, show seller details and never show blank related tiles.
  • Improved: pages no longer flash unstyled while loading, images are sized for the screen, and phones get edge-to-edge photos.
  • Improved: a logged-out visitor who taps Message, Offer, RSVP or Apply is asked to log in and returns with their draft kept.
  • New: “Move from another plugin” wizard. Bring listings over from Directorist, GeoDirectory, HivePress, WP Job Manager, The Events Calendar, Events Manager, Modern Events Calendar, EventON, Event Organiser, All-in-One Event Calendar, Sugar Calendar, Eventin or WP Event Manager in five friendly steps. It finds their data even when the old plugin is switched off, never changes it, runs in resumable batches and skips anything already moved.
  • New: old listing URLs keep working. Moved and CSV-imported listings redirect (301) from their old addresses, so links and search rankings carry over. Turn it off under Settings › SEO.
  • New: CSV import columns for opening hours (write them naturally, like “Mon-Fri 9-5; Sat 10am-2pm; Sun closed”), price level, services, amenities, booking links, the extra job fields and every marketplace field, plus an old_url column.
  • New: a friendly, dismissible note from the developer asking for a review, shown only on Nex Directory screens after a week of use.
  • Fixed: lost password and WordPress registration forms could silently do nothing while Nex Directory was active.
  • Fixed: event times in time zones such as Europe/London could show an hour late in some places.
  • Fixed: prices like “£65k” or “1,250” lost their scale; “Almost full” showed with nobody going; backwards date ranges and midnight closing hours.
  • Fixed: category and tag archives fell back to the theme layout; the owner analytics and boost pages could show raw shortcodes.
  • Accessibility: every page now scores 100 in Lighthouse accessibility, with labelled form fields, keyboard-friendly galleries and rails, and accent text that always meets contrast with any brand colour.
  • Faster: about half the database queries per page, by loading settings in one query and caching card categories.
  • Improved: card photos fill their frame inside Elementor layouts; tidier no-results page; the Map/List button no longer covers the last card.
  • Developer: nexdirectory_migration_sources filter and adapter interface, nexdirectory_migrated_listing action, nexdirectory_import_type_columns, nexdirectory_legacy_redirect_target and nexdirectory_redirect_legacy_urls filters.

1.5.0

  • Redesigns every public page with a new design system: spacing, type, cards, buttons, toasts with Undo, and reduced-motion support.
  • Adds site-type-specific behaviour for Local directory (opening hours and “Open now”), Jobs (pay, job type, closing date, Apply now) and Marketplace (condition, Reserved/Sold, Make an offer, delivery).
  • Adds 12 listing-page templates, including new Venue, Job and Product layouts, and 7 card styles.
  • Adds an app-like mobile layout with a bottom tab bar, bottom sheets and a sticky action bar.
  • Rebuilds the full-screen map with brand pins, a synced list and a draggable phone sheet.
  • Redesigns the organiser workspace and the WordPress dashboard, with a keyboard-friendly inbox.
  • Replaces the setup wizard with a shorter flow that asks what you’re building first.
  • Adds a live preview to Settings and a save bar that only appears when something changed.
  • Server-synced saved items for signed-in users, with a guest fallback.
  • Consistent, locale-aware dates, prices and counts across every screen.
  • Fixes many layout bugs, duplicate actions and wrong-type wording, and cleans up the sample content.

1.4.7

  • Fixes a WordPress admin CSS class conflict that could hide pending moderation submissions and User Management tables at desktop widths.
  • Corrects responsive onboarding labels and encoded punctuation in event titles.
  • Verifies the WordPress.org package on WordPress 7.1.
  • Keeps the WordPress.org package focused on maintenance fixes only, with no premium functionality or new external services added.

1.4.6

  • Removes PHP file creation from uploads-based private storage and routes demo media imports through WordPress media handling.
  • Preserves valid SMTP password characters while still keeping masked saved secrets unchanged.
  • Tightens frontend action nonces, moderation handlers, redirect sanitization, gallery input handling, and request-derived schema data.
  • Escapes generated plugin markup through WordPress wp_kses() allow-lists at output time.
  • Updates compatibility metadata for WordPress 7.0.4.

1.4.5

  • Rewrites key admin, onboarding, settings, and frontend notices in clearer, more natural language.
  • Improves settings explanations for setup templates, page links, submissions, uploads, notifications, and Chrome extension imports.
  • Keeps the unlimited publishing and optional Pro add-on messaging clear without confusing product or review wording.

1.4.4

  • Moves the maintained Tailwind source entry into docs/source so the release ZIP does not contain a build-tooling directory.
  • Updates source rebuild instructions to use explicit npx commands without requiring bundled package files.
  • Bumps release metadata for a clean WordPress.org resubmission package.

1.4.3

  • Removes “Free” from the public plugin name and bundled placeholder branding.
  • Removes prohibited local build tooling from the plugin package.
  • Stores plugin-created private files beneath uploads/nexdirectory using WordPress upload-directory APIs.
  • Adds earlier nonce checks and tighter sanitization for frontend submission, claim, report, contact, upload, and calendar flows.

1.4.2

  • Routes frontend login, registration, and password recovery through WordPress core authentication endpoints.
  • Removes the plugin-owned account creation/login handlers to preserve compatibility with security and membership plugins.

1.4.1

  • Uses WordPress-recognized nonce checks before reading submitted values in state-changing handlers.
  • Stops the demo importer from creating demo WordPress users or assigning roles.
  • Escapes generated filter-control markup at output.
  • Uses WordPress upload-directory APIs for plugin private-storage paths.

1.4.0

  • Confirms that Nex Directory has no three-listing, three-post, or three-event cap.
  • Keeps Events, Local Directory, Jobs, and Marketplace setup templates available.
  • Keeps core RSVP, waitlist, unified notifications, basic Needs Attention, and organizer privacy workflows in Free.
  • Keeps public site and organizer iCalendar subscriptions in Free.
  • Makes the official Chrome extension download prominent in the Free Connection Centre and release documentation.
  • Adds an in-plugin Free versus Pro comparison and separates licensed advanced implementations into the existing Nex Directory Pro add-on.
  • Hardens private-file cleanup and includes local license copies for bundled browser libraries.
  • Aligns WordPress.org packaging, source, and third-party notices with the actual Free bundle.

It copies details, dates in the right time zone, venues, contact details, opening hours, categories and images, never changes your old data, and redirects your old listing URLs so links and search rankings carry over. You can also import any CSV or JSON file, including opening hours written in plain English.

For agencies and developers

Nex Directory includes shortcodes, Elementor widgets, REST endpoints for approved integrations, filters and actions, and readable CSS and JavaScript with design tokens, so you can restyle it without fighting it. No build step is needed to install or run it.

Optional Chrome extension

The plugin includes a Chrome Extension setup screen for the official Nex Directory Scanner. It shows connection status, recent activity, policy checks, and a secure connection key you can rotate.

Official Nex Directory Chrome extension:

https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/nexdirectory-scanner/dnijcccaedhkbbekcbacgbhldmminpip

The extension is optional. Nex Directory opens the Chrome Web Store only when an administrator clicks the download link.

Optional Pro add-on

Nex Directory Pro is a separate add-on for sites that need more advanced workflows, such as AI-assisted setup, custom templates, advanced fields and filters, private attending calendars, ticketing, paid boosts, QR check-in, analytics exports, team tools, white-label controls, and search indexing hooks.

Those Pro tools and any services they use are not bundled in this WordPress.org plugin. The directory, event, submission, moderation, map, calendar, and member features listed here continue to work without Pro.

External services

Nex Directory avoids contacting outside providers unless a related optional feature is configured, shown on the page, or deliberately clicked. These notes explain what may be shared when you choose to use those features. Requests can include normal browser data such as IP address, browser details, and referrer, along with the feature-specific data described below.

NexDirectory.com and Chrome Web Store

NexDirectory.com receives normal browser request data only when an administrator clicks a product, documentation, or support link. The Chrome Web Store receives the same type of data after an administrator clicks the extension download link.

NexDirectory terms: https://nexdirectory.com/terms-of-service/
NexDirectory privacy: https://nexdirectory.com/privacy-policy/
Google terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
Google privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Google services

reCAPTCHA loads only after a site owner configures it; browser data and verification tokens are sent to Google. Google Maps and geocoding are used only when selected and can receive an API key, entered location, coordinates, or map position. Clicking “Directions” or “Open in Google Maps” on a listing opens Google Maps with that listing’s address or coordinates. Clicking “Google Calendar” sends the listing title, dates, description, and location to Google Calendar. Opening a Google Docs preview sends the document URL to Google Docs Viewer.

Google terms/privacy: https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
Google Maps terms: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms

Map, tile, and geocoding providers

Maps load their tiles from the provider the site owner selects: Esri (ArcGIS Online basemaps, used by the default Modern light, Minimal grey and Dark styles), OpenStreetMap, OSM France HOT, OpenTopoMap, Mapbox, Google Maps or a custom provider. Map/tile requests can include map position, tile coordinates, zoom level and entered location text. Server-side geocoding sends location text; Mapbox validation can send the configured token and style path.

OpenStreetMap policies/privacy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ and https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy
Nominatim policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/
OSM France terms: https://www.openstreetmap.fr/mentions-legales/
OpenTopoMap usage: https://opentopomap.org/about
Mapbox terms/privacy: https://www.mapbox.com/legal/tos and https://www.mapbox.com/legal/privacy/
Esri terms/privacy: https://www.esri.com/en-us/legal/terms/full-master-agreement and https://www.esri.com/en-us/privacy/overview

Calendar links

Clicking “Outlook” or “Office 365” in an add-to-calendar menu opens Microsoft Outlook on the web and sends the listing title, dates, description and location to Microsoft. Nothing is sent until a visitor clicks. (Google Calendar is covered under Google services above.)

Microsoft terms/privacy: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement

Web fonts (off by default)

The default font, Inter, is bundled with the plugin. If a developer enables the nexdirectory_load_remote_web_fonts filter to use another font, the visitor’s browser requests that font from Bunny Fonts (fonts.bunny.net), which receives normal browser request data.

Bunny Fonts terms/privacy: https://bunny.net/tos/ and https://bunny.net/privacy/

Media previews and sharing

When an owner adds YouTube or Vimeo media, the provider can receive normal browser request data when its thumbnail/player loads or a visitor opens it. Google Docs previews are covered above. Clicking a Facebook, X, LinkedIn or WhatsApp share control sends the public listing URL and, where supported, its title to that provider.

YouTube terms/privacy: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
Vimeo terms/privacy: https://vimeo.com/terms and https://vimeo.com/privacy
Facebook terms/privacy: https://www.facebook.com/terms/ and https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
X terms/privacy: https://x.com/en/tos and https://x.com/en/privacy
LinkedIn terms/privacy: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement and https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy
WhatsApp terms/privacy: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy

Source code and build tools

All plugin-owned PHP, JavaScript, and CSS needed to inspect and modify the release is included. No build step is required to install or run it.

Bundled third-party browser libraries are versioned upstream runtime files. Exact versions, licenses, and public source URLs are listed in docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md. The portable source and commands for regenerating the Tailwind utility bundle are in docs/SOURCE_AND_BUILD.md.
